name: stri_sub_all_replace
title: Replace multiple substrings and return the copy

origin.description: Alias of stri_sub_replace_all. Replace several substrings in each string and return the new vector.

arguments.text: Arguments passed to stri_sub_all<-: str, from, to, length, omit_na, and use_matrix.

arguments.name: replacement
arguments.text: Replacement strings. A plain character vector is wrapped into a list. Used when value is omitted.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Replacement strings. When both are passed, value is written.

origin.details: The installed function is the same object as stri_sub_replace_all. A non-positive from is rewritten to 1 and length is an exclusive end, so from = 0 and length = 3 on "hello" yields "Qlo".
origin.value: A character vector of the replaced strings.

arguments.name: args
arguments.text: Positional arguments of stri_sub_all_assign: str, from_, to, and length.

arguments.name: replacement
arguments.text: Replacement strings. A flat list is one character vector.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Replacement strings. When both are passed, value is written.

translation.details: The Python name is the same function object as stri_sub_replace_all. from_ is R's from. from_ = 0 and length = 3 on "hello" yields "Qlo".
translation.value: A list of the replaced strings.
translation.example:
from stringi.sub import stri_sub_all_replace
print(stri_sub_all_replace("hello", from_=0, length=3, replacement="Q"))
